q: A parent should be able to read a class resource but must not change or comment on it. Which role is best?
A colleague should be able to leave feedback on a Doc without directly editing the text. Which access level is best?
exp: Commenter allows feedback without full editing rights.

q: Two teachers need to revise a planning document together. Which access role should they have?
exp: Editors can directly modify the shared document.

q: A confidential planning document should be accessible only to named staff members. Which sharing approach is best?
choices: Anyone with the link as Editor

q: A file should be editable by two teachers but only viewable by students. What is the best setup?
exp: Different roles can be assigned based on each group's needs.

q: Which two practices are appropriate when sharing a file for team collaboration? (Select two.)
choices: Give edit access only to people who need to edit
exp: Appropriate permissions and clear naming support safe, manageable collaboration.

q: You want students to peer-review a document without rewriting the original text. Which role is best?
exp: Commenter supports feedback without direct rewriting.

q: A colleague says they cannot open a resource you shared. What should you check first?
choices: The file's sharing permissions and the account they are using
exp: Access problems are commonly caused by permissions or account mismatch.

q: A resource is intended for a small project team only. Which option best protects it?
choices: Keep General access Restricted and add team members

q: You want students to see a Slides presentation but not modify it. Which permission should you grant?
exp: Viewer is appropriate for read-only access.

q: A teacher accidentally gave a student Editor access instead of Viewer access. What should the teacher do?
choices: Change the student's access role to Viewer
exp: Changing the role corrects the permission without disrupting the file.

q: Which two choices are examples of applying least-privilege sharing? (Select two.)
choices: Give Viewer access when reading is enough
Give Editor access only when editing is required
Give everyone Editor access to avoid questions
exp: Least privilege means granting only the permissions necessary for the task.

q: A teacher wants a colleague to make edits but not take ownership of the file. Which role is appropriate?
exp: Editor grants edit rights without transferring ownership.

q: What is the best reason to avoid setting sensitive student information to 'Anyone with the link'?
choices: The link can be forwarded beyond the intended audience
exp: Link sharing can expand access beyond the intended audience.

q: A teacher is sharing a folder with a co-teacher who must add and edit files inside it. Which access level is most suitable?
exp: An Editor can work with files in the shared folder.

q: You need to stop a former collaborator from accessing a shared file. What should you do?
choices: Remove their access from Share settings
exp: Removing a person from the sharing list revokes their access.
